name: module-edit-autosave
description: 0.0.8 plan 2, M-1 to M-4 (the hello project, with files.autoSave afterDelay): a module interface is written function by function while its importer is open. Each pause with half a statement on the screen (the runner leaves the broken text up for 0.5 to 2.5 s) is written to disk once a second has passed since the last key, so clangd fails to build the module, over and over. 0.0.7 took the module's own file from clangd with its importers (RP1.1): one 'module-failed' diagnostic without a position instead of its real errors, and completion from mcppls's own engine, empty, until the next save handed it back -- in the reproduction 106 of 223 completions in the module being written were empty. The unit whose compile failed stays with clangd (M-1): the typed file never receives a 'module-failed' diagnostic. Its importer is still contained while the module does not compile, as a module that does not compile is, and its completion has the file's words (M-2): the probe line `int probe_value = 1; probe_v` inside main() must never get an empty answer. No status sample may say preparation-stalled (M-3), clangd is not restarted and no request times out. One typing check on the module interface, 30 s at 10 Hz, autosave 1000 ms after the last key (autosave-idle-ms); 2 s for the completions of both files, which are answered in tens of milliseconds.
